title: [Bug]: tracing clamps page.screencast capture size, padding the video with grey
body:
### Version

1.62.1

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone https://github.com/bdcarr/playwright-trace-clamps-screencast
2. `npm install`
3. `npm run test`

The same spec runs under two projects, one with `trace: 'off'` and one with `trace: 'on'`.
It records an entirely magenta page with:

    await page.screencast.start({ path, size: { width: 1260, height: 710 } });

with a viewport of 1680x946.

4. Open the two videos under test-results/:
   - ...-trace-off/video.webm  -> magenta fills the whole 1260x710 frame
   - ...-trace-on/video.webm   -> magenta occupies only the top-left 798x450; the rest is grey

Since the page is a solid colour, any grey area is padding.

### Expected behavior

With `size` passed to `screencast.start()`, the page should be scaled to fill the 1260x710 video
frame, regardless of whether tracing is enabled. This is what happens with `trace: 'off'`, and what
context-level `recordVideo: { size }` does in both cases.

### Actual behavior

With tracing enabled, the video is produced at the requested 1260x710 frame size, but the page is
captured at 800x450 and placed in the top-left corner, with the remaining ~60% of the frame filled
with grey.

### Additional context

800x450 is the 1680x946 viewport scaled to fit inside 800x600 — the hardcoded `kScreencastOptions`
used for trace screenshots. It appears the trace screencast and `page.screencast` share one
underlying capture, the smaller (trace) size wins, and `size` then only sets the output frame rather
than scaling the capture into it.

| path | `trace: 'off'` | `trace: 'on'` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `page.screencast.start({ size: 1260x710 })` | 1260x710, fills frame | 1260x710 frame, **page only 798x450, rest grey** |
| `page.screencast.start()` (no size) | 800x450, fills frame | 800x450, fills frame |
| `recordVideo: { size: 1260x710 }` | 1260x710, fills frame | 1260x710, fills frame |

So `recordVideo` is unaffected; only `page.screencast` is clamped.

There is no workaround while tracing is on, since the trace screencast size is not configurable —
the only way to get a full-resolution screencast is to disable tracing.

### Environment

  CPU: (12) arm64 Apple M2 Pro
